zh: 我们这个周末从奥克兰开车去汉密尔顿。
en: We're driving {down} to Hamilton from Auckland this weekend.
note: In New Zealand, down means south. Hamilton is south of Auckland, so you go down to Hamilton.

zh: 圣诞节我们要去北部，在派希亚租了一间度假屋。
en: We're going {up} north for Christmas. We've rented a bach in Paihia.
note: Up means north. "Up north" usually means Northland, the top of the North Island.

zh: 她昨天从基督城飞来奥克兰看我们。
en: She flew {up} to Auckland from Christchurch yesterday to see us.
note: Auckland is north of Christchurch, so people in the South Island come up to Auckland.

zh: 我们住在奥克兰，下个月要开车去旺格雷看我岳母。
en: We live in Auckland, and next month we're driving {up} to Whangārei to see my mother-in-law.
note: Whangārei is north of Auckland, so from Auckland you drive up to Whangārei.

zh: 你下班后要去北岸吗？能搭个便车吗？
en: Are you going {over|across} to the North Shore after work? Can I get a lift?
note: The North Shore is across the harbour from the city, so Aucklanders go over or across to the Shore.

zh: 我们周六坐渡轮去怀赫基岛。
en: We're catching the ferry {over|out} to Waiheke on Saturday.
note: Over is used for crossing water. Out also works, because Waiheke is out in the gulf, away from the city.

zh: 我哥哥去年搬到了澳大利亚的布里斯班。
en: My brother moved {across|over} the ditch to Brisbane last year.
note: "The ditch" is the Tasman Sea. Going across the ditch means going to Australia.

zh: 我今晚六点送妈妈去奥克兰机场。
en: I'm taking Mum {out|down} to Auckland Airport at six tonight.
note: Out means away from the centre. The airport is outside the city, and in Auckland it is also south, so down works too.

zh: 他们住在奥克兰西区，离市中心大概四十分钟。
en: They live {out} west, about forty minutes from the city.
note: "Out west" means West Auckland. Out is used for places away from the city centre.

zh: 你今天要去市中心吗？
en: Are you going {into} town today?
note: Into town means towards the city centre. "Town" here means the CBD, not another town.

zh: 我下班后去戴夫家坐一会儿。
en: I'm going to {pop round|pop over|nip round|nip over|go round|go over|head round|head over|drop round|duck round|duck over} to Dave's after work.
note: Round or over is used for visiting someone's home. Pop means go somewhere quickly or for a short time.

zh: 周六来我家吃晚饭吧。
en: Come {over|round} for dinner on Saturday.
note: "Come over" or "come round" means come to my place for a visit.

zh: 我去街角小店买点牛奶，很快就回来。
en: I'll {pop down|nip down|duck down|run down|go down|pop up|nip up|duck up|run up|go up|pop out|nip out|duck out|pop over|nip over|pop round|nip round|duck round} to the dairy and grab some milk.
note: For short local trips, down or up does not mean south or north. "Pop down to the dairy" just means go to the corner shop quickly.

zh: 超市就在这条路上，走几步就到。
en: The supermarket is just {up|down} the road.
note: "Up the road" and "down the road" both just mean a short distance along the road, not north or south.

zh: 我们周日晚上开车回家。
en: We're driving {back} home on Sunday night.
note: Back means returning to the place you came from, here your home.

zh: 她休完育儿假，下周一回来上班。
en: She's coming {back} to work next Monday after parental leave.
note: "Back to work" means returning to your job after time away.

zh: 他在惠灵顿开会，明天飞回奥克兰。
en: He's at a conference in Wellington, then he's flying {back} {up} to Auckland tomorrow.
note: Back shows he is returning, and up shows the direction: Auckland is north of Wellington.

zh: 我下周回来，到时候一起喝杯咖啡吧。
en: I'll be {back} in town next week, so let's grab a coffee.
note: "Back in town" means you have returned to the city where you live after being away.

zh: 我爸妈从汉密尔顿开车来奥克兰看宝宝。
en: My parents drove {up} from Hamilton to Auckland to see the baby.
note: Hamilton is south of Auckland, so the trip from Hamilton to Auckland is up.

zh: 今年夏天我们要去南岛玩两周。
en: We're heading {down} to the South Island for two weeks over summer.
note: The South Island is south of the North Island, so people always go down to it.

zh: 我们在奥克兰机场接上她，然后开车去了陶波。
en: We picked her up at Auckland Airport and drove {down} to Taupō.
note: Taupō is in the middle of the North Island, south of Auckland, so you drive down to Taupō.

zh: 我好多年没去岛屿湾了。
en: I haven't been {up} to the Bay of Islands for years.
note: The Bay of Islands is in Northland, near the top of the country, so you go up there.

zh: 高峰期过桥去北岸要四十分钟。
en: At rush hour it takes forty minutes to get {over|across} the bridge to the Shore.
note: Over and across are used for crossing something, like a bridge or a harbour.

zh: 他们周末常去皮哈海滩冲浪。
en: They often head {out} to Piha to surf at the weekend.
note: Piha is on the west coast, far from the city, so Aucklanders go out to Piha.

zh: 我们在罗托鲁瓦住了一晚，然后接着开到陶波。
en: We stayed a night in Rotorua, then carried on {down} to Taupō.
note: Taupō is south of Rotorua, so you carry on down to Taupō.

zh: 我住在基督城，下个月要去奥克兰出差。
en: I live in Christchurch, and next month I'm going {up} to Auckland for work.
note: From the South Island, Auckland is north, so you go up to Auckland.

zh: 我们从基督城经亚瑟隘口开车去了西海岸。
en: We drove {over|across} to the West Coast from Christchurch through Arthur's Pass.
note: Over or across is used when you cross mountains or water. From Christchurch you cross the Southern Alps to the Coast.

zh: 我们三月要飞去澳大利亚参加表妹的婚礼。
en: We're flying {over|across} to Aussie for my cousin's wedding in March.
note: Australia is across the Tasman Sea, so Kiwis go over or across to Aussie.

zh: 去年夏天我们从奥克兰去科罗曼德半岛露营了。
en: We went {over|down} to the Coromandel from Auckland for a camping trip last summer.
note: The Coromandel is across the Firth of Thames and a bit south of Auckland, so people say over or down.

zh: 我们住在汉密尔顿，所以周末常开车去拉格兰冲浪。
en: We live in Hamilton, so at weekends we often drive {out|over} to Raglan for a surf.
note: Raglan is a small beach town west of Hamilton, away from the city, so you go out to Raglan.

zh: 我们的邻居就住在这条街上。
en: Our neighbours live just {down|up} the street.
note: "Down the street" or "up the street" just means a little way along the same street.

zh: 我爸妈住在乡下，离城里大概一个小时。
en: My parents live {out} in the country, about an hour from town.
note: Out is used for places away from the city, like the country, the farm or the beach.

zh: 我们周日下午都在海边，你想来就过来。
en: We'll be {out|down} at the beach all Sunday afternoon if you want to join us.
note: Kiwis say "out at the beach" or "down at the beach". Neither means a compass direction here.

zh: 我周二从奥克兰飞去惠灵顿开会。
en: I'm flying {down} to Wellington from Auckland on Tuesday for a meeting.
note: Wellington is at the bottom of the North Island, so from Auckland you go down to Wellington.

zh: 这个周末我们要离开城里去露营。
en: We're getting {out} of town this weekend to go camping.
note: "Get out of town" means leave the city for a while, often for a break.

zh: 他住在城市另一头，开车去他家要半小时。
en: He lives {across} town, so it's half an hour's drive to his place.
note: "Across town" means on the other side of the same city.

zh: 惠灵顿人周末常翻过山去怀拉拉帕玩。
en: In Wellington, people often go {over} the hill to the Wairarapa for the weekend.
note: Wellingtonians say "over the hill" for the Wairarapa, because you drive over the Remutaka hill to get there.

zh: 我们从惠灵顿坐渡轮去了皮克顿。
en: We took the ferry {across|over} to Picton from Wellington.
note: Across or over is used for crossing water. The ferry crosses Cook Strait to Picton.

zh: 从奥克兰开车去陶朗加大概三个小时。
en: It's about three hours' drive {down} to Tauranga from Auckland.
note: Tauranga is south-east of Auckland, so Aucklanders go down to Tauranga.

zh: 从汉密尔顿去陶朗加玩一天很方便。
en: From Hamilton it's easy to nip {over} to Tauranga for the day.
note: From Hamilton, Tauranga is east, over the Kaimai Range, so people say over, not down.

zh: 我住在奥克兰，但我姐姐住在但尼丁，所以我只有圣诞节才能见到她。
en: I'm in Auckland, but my sister lives {down} in Dunedin, so I only see her at Christmas.
note: Dunedin is far south in the South Island, so from Auckland she lives down in Dunedin.

zh: 她从奥克兰搬到了皇后镇，说再也不回来了。
en: She moved {down} to Queenstown from Auckland and says she's never coming {back}.
note: Queenstown is in the South Island, so you move down there. Coming back means returning to Auckland.

zh: 我们去北部的路上在旺格雷停下吃了午饭。
en: We stopped in Whangārei for lunch on the way {up} north.
note: "On the way up north" means on the trip north to Northland.

zh: 我岳父母圣诞节要从惠灵顿过来，所以我们就待在奥克兰。
en: My in-laws are coming {up} from Wellington for Christmas, so we're staying in Auckland.
note: Wellington is south of Auckland, so people from Wellington come up to Auckland.

zh: 昨天下午我们去北岸看了个房子。
en: Yesterday afternoon we {went over|went across|headed over|headed across|drove over|drove across|popped over|nipped over} to the North Shore to look at a house.
note: You go over or across to the North Shore because it is on the other side of the harbour.

zh: 你什么时候有空来看看我们的新房子？
en: When can you {come round|come over|pop round|pop over|drop round|swing round|swing by} and see the new house?
note: "Come round" or "come over" means visit someone at their home.

zh: 他昨晚去他妈妈家吃饭了。
en: He {went round|went over|headed round|headed over|popped round|popped over|nipped round|nipped over} to his mum's for dinner last night.
note: "Go round to someone's" means visit their home. "His mum's" means his mum's house.

zh: 我们明天从奥克兰开车去罗托鲁瓦参加我外甥的生日会。
en: We're {driving down|heading down|going down|travelling down|traveling down} from Auckland to Rotorua tomorrow for my nephew's birthday.
note: Rotorua is south of Auckland, so from Auckland you drive down to Rotorua.

zh: 上周末他们开车去北地钓鱼了。
en: Last weekend they {drove up|went up|headed up|travelled up|traveled up} to Northland to go fishing.
note: Northland is the top of the North Island, so you always go up to Northland.

zh: 她刚从基督城搬到奥克兰。
en: She's just {moved up|come up} to Auckland from Christchurch.
note: Moving from Christchurch to Auckland is moving north, so you move up.

zh: 他每个月都从惠灵顿飞来奥克兰开会。
en: He {flies up|comes up} from Wellington for meetings in Auckland every month.
note: From Wellington, Auckland is north, so he flies up.

zh: 他的航班十点到，我们早点去机场吧。
en: His flight lands at ten, so let's {head out|go out|drive out|get out} to the airport early.
note: Airports are usually outside the city centre, so people go out to the airport.

zh: 周日我们去西区的怀塔克雷山脉走了一趟丛林步道。
en: On Sunday we {headed out|went out|drove out} west to the Waitākere Ranges for a bush walk.
note: "Out west" means West Auckland, away from the city centre.

zh: 我要去市中心办点事，你需要带什么吗？
en: I'm {going into|heading into|popping into|nipping into|driving into} town to run a few errands. Do you need anything?
note: "Into town" means towards the city centre, where the shops and offices are.

zh: 我们回到奥克兰后给你打电话。
en: I'll give you a call when we {get back} to Auckland.
note: "Get back" means arrive home again after a trip.

zh: 他们周五晚上从惠灵顿开车去罗托鲁瓦。
en: On Friday night they're driving {up} to Rotorua from Wellington.
note: Up or down depends on where you start. Rotorua is north of Wellington, so from Wellington you drive up.

zh: 她是南岛人，在因弗卡吉尔长大。
en: She's from {down} south. She grew up in Invercargill.
note: "Down south" usually means the South Island. Invercargill is at the very bottom of it.

zh: 我每天早上从北岸过桥进城上班。
en: Every morning I come {over|across} the bridge {into} the city from the Shore.
note: Over or across is for crossing the bridge, and into is for going towards the city centre.

zh: 我表哥要从悉尼过来住一周。
en: My cousin's coming {over|across} from Sydney for a week.
note: Over or across is used for trips between New Zealand and Australia, because you cross the Tasman Sea.

zh: 周六我们去怀赫基岛吃个午饭吧。
en: Let's {pop over|nip over|head over|go over|pop out|nip out|head out|go out} to Waiheke for lunch on Saturday.
note: Pop over means make a quick trip. Over is used because you cross the water to Waiheke.
